TOPIC: Digital Adoption Platforms (DAPs) as the SOFTWARE alternative to human adoption consultants. Players: WalkMe, Whatfix, Pendo, Userlane, Userpilot, Appcues (and any newer AI-driven ones). How do they position "adoption" and specifically the STORY of guiding a user IN-APP, step by step (walkthroughs, tooltips, in-app guidance)?

Do real web searches + fetch homepages/product pages:
- "WalkMe digital adoption platform" homepage tagline
- "Whatfix in-app guidance adoption"
- "Pendo adoption" / "Userlane in-app guidance"
- their exact hero taglines and product positioning copy

For EACH player (aim for 5-7):
- Name + what it is + exact URL
- NARRATIVE: verbatim hero tagline + positioning copy (quote REAL sentences in quotes), how they frame the "in-app guidance / walkthrough / guide the user step-by-step" story, the emotional/strategic angle, and WHO they talk to (software vendor? enterprise IT? L&D?).
- Explicitly CONTRAST their "in-app guidance" narrative — is it generic tooltips overlaid on software, or personalized? Note whether the guidance is tied to the SOFTWARE (any user) vs tied to the individual PERSON.

Quote REAL copy from fetched pages. No fabrication. Return structured ENGLISH markdown.

- agent-browser: Browse the web for any task — research topics, read articles, interact with web apps, fill forms, take screenshots, extract data, and test web pages. Use whenever a browser would be useful, not just when the user explicitly asks.
- frontend-engineer: Pro frontend engineering discipline. Enforces build-test-verify workflow for every web project. Never declare done until the site is built, tested, responsive, accessible, and visually verified in a real browser. Use alongside vercel-cli for production-quality deployments.
- onecli-gateway: OneCLI Gateway: transparent HTTPS proxy that injects stored credentials into outbound calls. You MUST use this skill when the user asks you to read emails, check calendar, access GitHub repos, create issues, check Stripe payments, or interact with ANY external service or API. Do NOT use browser extensions or OAuth CLI tools. Make HTTP requests directly; the gateway injects credentials automatically.
- self-customize: Customize your own agent — add capabilities, install packages, add MCP servers, edit code or CLAUDE.md. Use when the user asks you to add a feature, install a tool, or modify how you work. For non-trivial code changes, delegate to a builder agent via create_agent.
- slack-formatting: Format messages for Slack using mrkdwn syntax. Use when responding to Slack channels (folder starts with "slack_" or JID contains slack identifiers).
- vercel-cli: Deploy apps to Vercel. Use when asked to deploy, ship, or publish a web application, or manage Vercel projects, domains, and environment variables.
- welcome: Introduce yourself to a newly connected channel. Triggered automatically when a channel is first wired. Send a friendly greeting and brief overview of what you can do.
- whatsapp-formatting: Format messages for WhatsApp, including mentions that render as real WhatsApp tags. Use when responding in a WhatsApp conversation (platform_id / chatJid ends with @s.whatsapp.net or @g.us).
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Based on the search results, here's what the 2026 digital adoption landscape reveals about AI-powered in-app guidance versus generic tooltips:

## Key Distinction: Personalized vs. Generic Approaches

Generic walkthroughs and static help content treat all users the same, leading to irrelevant guidance for some and insufficient support for others. The market is clearly moving away from one-size-fits-all overlays.

## AI-Powered Personalization in 2026

Modern platforms emphasize behavioral personalization over static tooltips:

An AI-powered product adoption platform is software that drives users toward successful, sustained use of a product by detecting behavioral signals in real time and delivering contextual guidance automatically, rather than relying on pre-scripted flows that a human configured in advance.

The leading platforms now use AI to recommend optimal experiences, generate content, analyze performance patterns, and personalize guidance based on real-time behavior. This is the difference between manually building every flow and having a system that continuously optimizes for you.

## Role-Based and Individual Personalization

Use segmentation and user roles to personalize guidance across departments. More sophisticated platforms go further: guidance adapts to an individual user's role, skill level, and current workflow.

## Proactive vs. Reactive Guidance

A rule-based DAP fires guidance based on rules a human configured in advance, even if it uses AI to write the copy. An AI-powered adoption platform infers when a user needs help from real-time behavioral signals, including situations no one scripted for, and reaches users who never ask.

The consensus among leading 2026 platforms is that personalized, context-aware guidance driven by AI behavioral analysis significantly outperforms generic tooltip overlays in driving actual adoption outcomes.

# Digital Adoption Platforms (DAPs): The Software Alternative to Human Adoption Consultants

## The Category Story (2026)

DAPs sell one core promise: instead of paying human trainers/consultants to teach people software, you overlay a **software guidance layer** on top of any application that walks users through it in-app. The universal narrative beats are: *don't send people to training → guide them inside the tool, at the moment of need → measure adoption → prove ROI.*

A key **2026 shift** frames the competitive story: the category is moving from **rule-based, pre-scripted overlays** (a human builds every tooltip/flow in advance, same for everyone) toward **AI-inferred, behavioral guidance** (the system detects when a user is stuck from real-time signals and reaches users "who never ask"). This is the exact fault line your topic cares about — guidance tied to the *software* (any user hitting a screen) vs. guidance adapted to the *individual person*.

**Crucial structural point for your framing:** almost every DAP guides based on **where the user is in the software** (which screen, which field, which role-segment), *not* on who the person is as an individual with their own goals and history. The guidance lives on the app, not on the person. Even the "personalized" claims are mostly **role/segment-based** (e.g. "show sales this flow, show HR that one"), not a persistent per-person agent. That is the gap.

---

## 1. WalkMe — the enterprise-IT incumbent
**What it is:** The original enterprise DAP; a guidance/automation layer overlaid on enterprise apps (SAP, Salesforce, Workday, ServiceNow, Dynamics). Acquired by SAP.
**URL:** https://www.walkme.com/

**Verbatim hero:** *"WalkMe turns AI potential into AI performance."*
**Subhead:** *"WalkMe is the critical layer that makes enterprise AI work."*
**In-app guidance story:** Guides users through workflows *"inside the tools they already use. No training class. No help desk ticket."* Older category copy: on-screen *"Walk-Thrus — dynamic step-by-step instructions,"* a *"guidance layer added on top of any existing website, software or online platform."* It *"overlays on any application, identifies where critical workflows break, and then provides personalized guidance and automation."*
**Angle:** Kill training classes and help-desk tickets; prove AI/software ROI to the enterprise.
**Who they talk to:** **Enterprise IT / transformation leaders**, plus dept heads (Sales, HR, Customer Care). Buyer is the org rolling out software to employees.
**Guidance tied to software or person?** **Software.** The overlay sits on the application and fires by screen/workflow break. "Personalized" = role/context within the workflow, not a per-person agent.

---

## 2. Whatfix — the "in-app guidance" purebred
**What it is:** Enterprise DAP with the most literal "in-app guidance" positioning; strong L&D/change-management tilt.
**URL:** https://whatfix.com/

**Verbatim hero:** *"Increase user adoption with in-app guidance."*
**Subhead:** *"In-app guidance. Hands-on simulations. Actionable analytics. One unified platform to drive adoption and maximize ROI."*
**In-app guidance story:** Contextual *"Flows, Smart Tips, Pop-Ups, and Task Lists to standardize task execution and enable faster onboarding"* across web, desktop, mobile. Category line: *"empower anyone, anywhere to have scalable success with technology they use every day."*
**Angle:** Replace one-time training with continuous, contextual, in-flow help; scale change management.
**Who they talk to:** **L&D and HR** first, then Sales and Product; regulated industries (banking, healthcare, insurance, pharma, public sector). 700+ orgs.
**Guidance tied to software or person?** **Software**, with role/segment personalization. Flows are authored on the app screens; users get them by role/segment, not as individuals.

---

## 3. Pendo — analytics-first, adoption-second
**What it is:** Product-analytics platform that bundles in-app guides; positions adoption as the outcome of understanding behavior.
**URL:** https://www.pendo.io/

**Verbatim hero:** *"Close the gap between AI spend and AI adoption."*
**Subhead:** *"Pendo captures user behavior across your software and agents, identifies where users struggle, and puts that context to work—so your AI gets smarter in real time and every user gets a better experience."*
**In-app guides copy:** *"Help users right where they need it."* Guides *"speed up onboarding and adoption with relevant, contextual in-app messages"*; with *"conditional logic built into your guides, you can deliver tailored content and next steps that match individual needs."* AI authoring via *"Leo, Pendo's conversational interface."*
**Angle:** Data → insight → guided action. "Know what users love, where they struggle, what they ignore. Guide them to value."
**Who they talk to:** **Product teams** primarily, plus IT/enterprise deploying software and AI agents.
**Guidance tied to software or person?** **Software + behavior.** Closest to "individual" via conditional logic that adapts steps to a user's choices — but still triggered by in-product behavior on the app, not a standing personal agent that knows the human across contexts.

---

## 4. Userlane — regulated-industry, "put people at the heart"
**What it is:** Software adoption platform aimed squarely at regulated enterprises; leans on a human/people framing.
**URL:** https://www.userlane.com/

**Verbatim hero:** *"Remove Friction / Reduce Cost / Improve Adoption"*
**Subhead:** *"The intelligence to see the impact of your software and AI. The assistance to help your people get work done."*
**In-app guidance story:** Help *"directly within applications through contextual assistance — including AI-powered answers, structured workflow guidance, and automated processes — rather than relying on separate training sessions that users forget quickly."* Solution page: *"Software adoption, made easy"*; guidance *"from first click to full adoption."* Campaign line: *"Put people at the heart of digital transformation."*
**Angle:** Training you forget vs. real-time in-workflow support; ROI justification for expensive implementations.
**Who they talk to:** **Enterprise IT / ops in regulated industries** (healthcare, manufacturing, financial services, insurance, energy, public sector).
**Guidance tied to software or person?** **Software.** Despite the "people at the heart" language, guidance is workflow/role-structured on the app; "people" is the emotional frame, not per-individual personalization.

---

## 5. Userpilot — PLG / product-growth, no-code
**What it is:** Product-growth platform for SaaS teams; in-app onboarding + analytics + monetization.
**URL:** https://userpilot.com/

**Verbatim hero:** *"Product Analytics and Onboarding Platform for User Monetization."*
**Subhead:** *"Userpilot helps product and growth teams turn user signals into activation, adoption, retention, and revenue."*
**In-app guidance story:** Build *"in-app onboarding flows without code"* with *"tooltips, banners, spotlights, and contextual nudges"*; *"launch, iterate, and optimize without a single dev ticket."* 2026 addition: *"Lia: the only platform in this category with a project-based AI agent that automates the full insight-to-action loop."*
**Angle:** Ship growth experiences without engineering; guide users to value → revenue.
**Who they talk to:** **Product management, growth, PMM, UX, CS** at ~1,200+ SaaS companies. Buyer is the **software vendor**, guiding *their own customers*.
**Guidance tied to software or person?** **Software**, segment-personalized. The AI ("Lia") automates building flows, not being a personal companion to each end-user.

---

## 6. Appcues — onboarding-first, human/emotional voice
**What it is:** Product-led onboarding and adoption tool; warmest, most human brand voice in the set.
**URL:** https://www.appcues.com/

**Verbatim hero:** *"Build experiences that move people."*
**Subhead:** *"Meet customers at every stage with a platform built to drive outcomes."*
**Other real copy:** *"Adoption is where attention becomes habit."* Helps customers *"find their footing, hit their first wins, and keep coming back"*; *"turn first wins into routines users return to"* and *"move customers from one feature to many."* No-code: build/test/publish *"without waiting on engineering."*
**Angle:** Emotional/habit framing — attention → habit, first win → routine. Onboarding as the relationship's opening move.
**Who they talk to:** **Product, growth, and CS teams** at SaaS companies guiding their own users.
**Guidance tied to software or person?** **Software**, segment-driven ("personalized, segment-driven messaging delivered at critical moments"). Personalization = segment + lifecycle stage, not per-individual identity.

---

## 7. The AI-native shift (Whatfix AI, Apty, and the 2026 framing)
Rather than one clean new logo, the newer story is **AI-native repositioning** across the field, articulated most sharply by analysts and challengers:
- The contrast copy: *"Generic walkthroughs and static help content treat all users the same, leading to irrelevant guidance."*
- The new claim: *"An AI-powered adoption platform infers when a user needs help from real-time behavioral signals, including situations no one scripted for, and reaches users who never ask"* — versus *"a rule-based DAP [that] fires guidance based on rules a human configured in advance."*
- Aspirational personalization: *"guidance adapts to an individual user's role, skill level, and current workflow."*

**Sources:** https://userpilot.com/blog/digital-adoption-platforms/ , https://apty.ai/blog/best-digital-adoption-platforms/ , https://whatfix.com/blog/ai-in-digital-adoption-programs/

---

## The Contrast That Matters For Your Narrative

| Player | Hero framing | In-app guidance form | Primary buyer | Tied to… |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| WalkMe | "AI potential into AI performance" | Walk-Thrus overlaid on enterprise apps | Enterprise IT | **Software** |
| Whatfix | "Increase adoption with in-app guidance" | Flows, Smart Tips, Task Lists | L&D / HR | **Software** (role) |
| Pendo | "Close the gap between AI spend and adoption" | Behavior-triggered guides + conditional logic | Product | **Software + behavior** |
| Userlane | "Put people at the heart" | Contextual workflow guidance | Regulated-IT | **Software** |
| Userpilot | "…Platform for User Monetization" | No-code tooltips/nudges | SaaS product/growth | **Software** (segment) |
| Appcues | "Build experiences that move people" | Segment-driven onboarding flows | SaaS product/CS | **Software** (segment) |
| AI-native 2026 | "Reaches users who never ask" | Behavioral, inferred guidance | Enterprise + product | **Software behavior** (aspiring to person) |

**The load-bearing insight:** every one of these guides the user relative to **the software** — the screen they're on, the workflow step, at best their *role/segment*. Even the AI-native pitch personalizes by *behavior signals inside the app*, not by a durable model of the *individual person* that follows them across everything they do. The guidance is a layer on the **product**; nobody in this category owns a layer on the **person**. Whoever attaches step-by-step guidance to the *human* (their goals, history, cross-app life) rather than to *a piece of software* is telling a story the whole DAP category structurally cannot.
